info.name: Codevibe Sign HTTP API
info.description:
Send documents for signature, sign them, seal the PDF and verify it.

Generated from the OpenAPI document. Set `baseUrl` and `apiKey` first.

item.name: Envelopes
item.description:
An envelope is one signing job: its documents, the people who act on them, the fields
they fill and where it stands. Create, change, send, withdraw and list envelopes.
Sender API key required.

query.description: Case-insensitive text anywhere in the title.

request.description:
List envelopes

The caller's workspace's envelopes, newest first, one page at a time. Pass the
`nextCursor` of a page as `cursor` to get the next one. Each row is a summary without
fields or values; get the envelope for those.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.

request.description:
Create an envelope

Creates a draft with its documents, recipients and fields, and sends it at once when
`send` is `true`. Send the PDFs either as base64 in JSON, or as a multipart upload with
the envelope JSON in a form field named `envelope` and the files as `documents`.

The example carries a real one-page PDF, so it works as it is against a sandbox.

Each PDF is checked: at most 20 MB by default, at most 20 per envelope, and it must
open as a PDF. Field boxes are in PDF points from the top-left corner of the page and
must fit on it.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.

request.description:
Create an envelope

Creates a draft with its documents, recipients and fields, and sends it at once when
`send` is `true`. Send the PDFs either as base64 in JSON, or as a multipart upload with
the envelope JSON in a form field named `envelope` and the files as `documents`.

The example carries a real one-page PDF, so it works as it is against a sandbox.

Each PDF is checked: at most 20 MB by default, at most 20 per envelope, and it must
open as a PDF. Field boxes are in PDF points from the top-left corner of the page and
must fit on it.

Get an envelope

The envelope with its documents, recipients, fields and the values entered so far.

Change a draft

Changes a draft envelope. Only the properties you send change. `recipients` and
`fields`, when sent, replace the whole list: pass a recipient's `id` to keep it (its
signing order and details are updated), leave it out to remove it. Fields name their
recipient by `key` or `id` and their document by `id` or position (`"0"`).
Documents cannot be changed; create a new envelope instead. Send `"message": null`
to remove the message.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.

request.description:
Send a draft

Sends the draft. In sequential routing the recipients with the lowest `order` get their
signing links; in parallel routing everyone does. Viewers get a copy once it is complete.
The envelope needs at least one signer or approver, and every signer needs a signature
field.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.

request.description:
Withdraw an envelope

Withdraws a sent envelope that is not yet final. Signing links stop working and
recipients already invited are told it was withdrawn.

item.name: Recall a sent envelope to edit it

request.description:
Recall a sent envelope to edit it

Voids a sent or in-progress envelope with the reason "Recalled to correct" (and your
note), exactly like `void`: links stop and everyone already invited is told. Then
creates a new draft with the same documents (the original files), recipients, fields,
title, message and reminders, and an expiry of the same length from now. Signatures
already given are not carried over; everyone signs again. The old envelope records
`envelope.recalled` with `replacementId`; the draft's `envelope.created` has
`recalledFrom`.

Revise a declined envelope

Copies a declined envelope to a new draft, like `recall`, so you can address the
decline and send again. The declined envelope stays declined and unchanged; it
records `envelope.revised` with `replacementId`, and the draft's `envelope.created`
has `revisedFrom`. Set `changeNote` on the draft to tell recipients what changed.

item.name: Recipients
item.description:
The people on an envelope. Remind them, correct a mistyped address, or get a signing
link to pass on yourself. Sender API key required.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.

request.description:
Remind recipients

Mails a reminder with a fresh signing link to everyone whose turn it is, or to the one
recipient named. Each recipient gets at most one reminder or invitation every 15
minutes; manual reminders do not count against the automatic ones.

item.name: Get a signing link to pass on yourself

request.description:
Get a signing link to pass on yourself

A fresh signing link for a recipient whose turn it is, for when emails do not reach
them. No email is sent. Their earlier links stop working, so only the newest one
does. A one-time code still applies when the recipient signs with one. The audit
trail records `recipient.link_shared` with who took the link, never the link itself.
At most 5 links per recipient per hour. The link is in this response only and is never
stored in clear, so an `Idempotency-Key` is ignored: a retry gives a new link.

item.name: Correct a recipient who has not acted

request.description:
Correct a recipient who has not acted

Changes the name, email or phone of a recipient on a sent envelope who has not signed,
approved or declined. Role, order and fields stay. Their earlier links stop working.
When it is their turn and the email or phone changed, the new address is invited at
once; a name change sends nothing unless `resend` is true. Recorded as
`recipient.corrected` with the old and new values. Someone who has acted cannot be
changed (`INVALID_STATE` with `details.reason: acted`); recall the envelope instead.

item.name: Documents
item.description:
The PDFs of an envelope: replace a draft's file, download the original or the sealed
copy, and check the seal. Sender API key required.

query.description: `original`, `sealed` (fails with `INVALID_STATE` until sealing has finished) or `certificate` (fails with `INVALID_STATE` when the certificate is the last page of the sealed file).

request.description:
Download a PDF

The sealed PDF once the envelope is complete, otherwise the original. Ask for one of
them with `version`. A document signed with Aadhaar eSign is one file too: the
certificate page goes on before the signer signs, so the Aadhaar eSign and the seal
cover it. Only an Aadhaar eSign started before that change has its certificate as a
sealed file of its own: `version=certificate`.

Replace a draft's document

Uploads a new version of one document of a draft, as multipart (`document`, optional
`name`) or JSON (`name`, `content` in base64). Fields stay where they are when their
page still exists and they fit on it; the others are moved onto the nearest page and
listed in `movedFields`, so you can check them before sending.

Replace a draft's document

Uploads a new version of one document of a draft, as multipart (`document`, optional
`name`) or JSON (`name`, `content` in base64). Fields stay where they are when their
page still exists and they fit on it; the others are moved onto the nearest page and
listed in `movedFields`, so you can check them before sending.

Verify the sealed PDF

Runs the seal check on the stored sealed file against the operator certificate and any
older certificates the server trusts.

item.name: Audit trail
item.description:
The hash-chained audit log of an envelope and the signing certificate built from it.
Sender API key required.

request.description:
Audit log

Every action on the envelope, oldest first, and whether the hash chain is intact: each
event's `hash` is `sha256(prevHash + canonical(event))` and the last one must equal the
envelope's `auditHead`.

Signing certificate

What the certificate page of the sealed PDF shows, as JSON: the hash of each document
before and after sealing, each recipient with the authentication they used and every
action they took, and the head of the audit chain.

Audit trail as a PDF

The envelope's audit trail as a PDF, the same file the completed-copy email carries:
the envelope, the SHA-256 of each document before and after signing, each recipient
with the method they used (an Aadhaar eSign names its provider), and every event with
its time in the workspace's time zone and UTC, who acted and the network address it
came from, then the head of the hash chain.

item.name: Templates
item.description:
A template is an envelope without the people: its PDFs, the roles that act on them
(Employee, HR), the fields each role fills and the settings. Make an envelope from one by
saying who takes each role. Sender API key required.

query.description: Case-insensitive text anywhere in the name.

request.description:
List templates

The caller's workspace's templates, newest first, one page at a time. Pass the
`nextCursor` of a page as `cursor` to get the next one. Each row is a summary; get the
template for its documents, roles and fields.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.

request.description:
Create a template

Stores the PDFs with the roles, fields and settings to reuse. Send the PDFs either as
base64 in JSON, or as a multipart upload with the template JSON in a form field named
`template` and the files as `documents`.

Fields name their role by its `key` in the same request. Each PDF is checked like an
envelope's, and field boxes must fit on their page.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.

request.description:
Create a template

Stores the PDFs with the roles, fields and settings to reuse. Send the PDFs either as
base64 in JSON, or as a multipart upload with the template JSON in a form field named
`template` and the files as `documents`.

Fields name their role by its `key` in the same request. Each PDF is checked like an
envelope's, and field boxes must fit on their page.

Get a template

The template with its documents, roles, fields and settings.

Change a template

Only the properties you send change. `roles` and `fields`, when sent, replace the
existing ones; give a role its `id` to keep it. Fields you do not resend must still
have their role. The documents of a template cannot be changed: create a new template
instead. Envelopes already made from the template are not affected.

Delete a template

Removes the template and its stored PDFs for good. Envelopes already made from it keep
their own copies and are not affected.

item.name: Create an envelope from a template

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.

request.description:
Create an envelope from a template

Makes an envelope with the template's documents, fields and settings, and the people
you name for its roles. `roles` is keyed by role name (case does not matter) or role
id, and every role needs a person. `prefill` sets text fields by their label or id
before anyone signs. The envelope is a draft unless `send` is `true`, and from then on
it is an ordinary envelope: `metadata.templateId` says where it came from.

Counts towards the same per-minute limit as creating envelopes.

item.name: Verification
item.description:
Check that a PDF is a document this server sealed and that nothing changed since.
Public: no API key, like the certificate page inside every sealed file. Limited per
client address.

request.description:
Verify a PDF

Upload a PDF to learn whether it is exactly a document this server sealed. The file is
read in memory, checked against the server's seal certificate and dropped: nothing
about it is stored. Send it as a multipart upload in a form field named `file`, or as
the raw body with `Content-Type: application/pdf`.

`checks` lists each check in order; the first that fails is the `reason`, and the
ones after it are `null` because they were not reached. For a valid file the answer
also names its envelope with the signers and the audit trail: the same facts the
certificate page inside the file prints, with contacts masked.

No API key is needed. Each client address may make 30 checks in 10 minutes by default,
and a file may be up to 20 MB.

variable.description: SHA-256 of the sealed PDF, 64 hexadecimal characters.

request.description:
Verify by SHA-256

The same answer without uploading the file: send the SHA-256 of the PDF you hold. The
server looks for a document it sealed with exactly that hash and checks its own stored
copy. A hash it never sealed answers `valid: false` with `unknown_document`, which is
also what a changed file gets, since any change gives another hash.

No API key is needed. It shares the per-address limit of the upload.

item.name: Signing
item.description:
What the recipient's browser calls. `{token}` is the signing token from the link,
or the literal `link` to use the token held in the `cvsign_link` cookie.

request.description:
Follow the envelope after signing

For a recipient who has signed or approved. The submit call hands back a receipt, as
the `cvsign_receipt` cookie and the `X-Sign-Receipt` header, valid for 7 days. With it
the recipient can see where the envelope stands, how many people it is still waiting
for (not who), and which documents are sealed and ready to download. The signing link
itself stops working once the recipient has acted.

query.description: `certificate` for the signing certificate of a document whose `certificate` is `true` in the receipt, `audit-trail` for the envelope's audit trail as a PDF once it is complete. Leave out for the signed document.

request.description:
Download your signed copy

The sealed PDF, once everyone has acted and the seal is applied. Before that the
answer is `INVALID_STATE`; poll `GET /v1/sign/receipt` until the document's `sealed`
is `true`.

item.name: Download a signed copy from its email link

query.description: The signed value from the download link in the completed-copy email.
`certificate` for the signing certificate of a document whose `certificate` is `true` in the receipt, `audit-trail` for the envelope's audit trail as a PDF. Leave out for the signed document.

request.description:
Download a signed copy from its email link

The link in a completed-copy email whose sealed files were not attached, because they
were too large or could not be read. It names one recipient of one completed
envelope and works for 30 days. Nothing else is needed to call it.

header.description: For recipients who sign with a one-time code, after otp/verify.

variable.description:
The signing token from the link (43 base64url characters), or `link` to use the
token in the `cvsign_link` cookie. Anything else is refused with `TOKEN_INVALID`.

request.description:
Open a signing session

The envelope basics, the recipient, their own fields and values, and what they still
need to do. For recipients who sign with a one-time code, `otpRequired` is `true` and
`authenticated` says whether a valid session came with the request. Until it is
`true` the answer holds only what the invitation email already said: `message` and
`changeNote` are `null`, `documents`, `fields` and `values` are empty and the email
address is masked. Read it again after `otp/verify`. `canAct` is `false` while it is
someone else's turn.

header.description: For recipients who sign with a one-time code, after otp/verify.

variable.description:
The signing token from the link (43 base64url characters), or `link` to use the
token in the `cvsign_link` cookie. Anything else is refused with `TOKEN_INVALID`.

request.description:
Download the original PDF

The document to sign. Recipients who sign with a one-time code must verify it first.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.

variable.description:
The signing token from the link (43 base64url characters), or `link` to use the
token in the `cvsign_link` cookie. Anything else is refused with `TOKEN_INVALID`.

request.description:
Send a one-time code

Sends a new six-digit code by email or SMS, valid for 10 minutes, and replaces the
previous one. At most 5 codes per 15 minutes and 10 per recipient over the envelope's
life; after that the answer is `OTP_LOCKED` with `details.reason: "too_many_codes"`
and the sender has to send the envelope again.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.

variable.description:
The signing token from the link (43 base64url characters), or `link` to use the
token in the `cvsign_link` cookie. Anything else is refused with `TOKEN_INVALID`.

request.description:
Verify the one-time code

Checks the code. On success the server sets a 30-minute `cvsign_session` cookie
(HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, path `/v1/sign`) and also returns the session, which you
can send as `X-Sign-Session` instead. Five wrong guesses lock the code (`OTP_LOCKED`);
ask for a new one.

item.name: Record that the document was opened

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.
For recipients who sign with a one-time code, after otp/verify.

variable.description:
The signing token from the link (43 base64url characters), or `link` to use the
token in the `cvsign_link` cookie. Anything else is refused with `TOKEN_INVALID`.

request.description:
Record that the document was opened

Marks the recipient as having viewed the document. Call it when the page shows the
document, not when the link is opened, so mail scanners that follow links change
nothing.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.
For recipients who sign with a one-time code, after otp/verify.

variable.description:
The signing token from the link (43 base64url characters), or `link` to use the
token in the `cvsign_link` cookie. Anything else is refused with `TOKEN_INVALID`.

request.description:
Sign or approve

Submits the recipient's field values and their consent to sign electronically. Signers
must fill every required field; approvers send an empty `values` list. When the last
required recipient acts, the envelope completes and the sealed PDF is produced.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.
For recipients who sign with a one-time code, after otp/verify.

variable.description:
The signing token from the link (43 base64url characters), or `link` to use the
token in the `cvsign_link` cookie. Anything else is refused with `TOKEN_INVALID`.

request.description:
Decline

Declines to sign. The envelope becomes `declined` and everyone already invited is told.

variable.description:
The signing token from the link (43 base64url characters), or `link` to use the
token in the `cvsign_link` cookie. Anything else is refused with `TOKEN_INVALID`.

request.description:
Follow an Aadhaar eSign

Where the recipient's Aadhaar eSign stands. While it is `pending` the server also
asks the provider, at most once every few seconds, so the page the signer comes
back to moves on even when the provider's callback is late. Unlike the other signing
routes it still answers after the recipient has signed, and then hands out the
receipt for `GET /v1/sign/receipt`.

header.description:
Any unique string, up to 255 characters. A retry with the same key and body within
24 hours returns the first response. The same key with a different body is a
`VALIDATION` error; while the first request is still running, `CONFLICT`.

variable.description:
The signing token from the link (43 base64url characters), or `link` to use the
token in the `cvsign_link` cookie. Anything else is refused with `TOKEN_INVALID`.

request.description:
Start an Aadhaar eSign

For a recipient with `auth: aadhaar`, in place of `submit`. Takes the same body:
the recipient's field values and their consent. The server draws the values on the
document, asks the eSign provider to sign that file and answers the provider's
signing page; send the signer there. The recipient becomes `signed` once the
provider reports the signature. Asking again while an attempt is open answers the
same page.

variable.description: The signing token from the email.

request.description:
Open a signing link

Where signing links point. Stores the token in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict
`cvsign_link` cookie (path `/v1/sign`, at most 24 hours) and redirects to the signing
page, whose URL carries no token. The page then calls `/v1/sign/link/...` from the same
origin. An unknown or used token clears the cookie and redirects all the same, adding
`?state=` with the reason (`signed`, `completed`, `declined`, `voided`, `expired` or
`invalid`) and, when the envelope is known, `&w=<workspaceId>` so the page can explain
it in the sender's brand. This route only reads: opening a link does not mark the
document as viewed.

item.name: Provider callbacks
item.description:
Where an Aadhaar eSign provider reports what became of a signing request. Called by
the provider, never by your code. Each callback is verified with the credentials of
the workspace that started the request.

variable.description: The eSign provider's name, for example `leegality`.

request.description:
Receive an eSign provider's callback

Set this address as the webhook of your eSign provider account. The body names the
signing request; the server finds the workspace that started it and verifies the
body with that workspace's provider credentials before acting on it. Repeats change
nothing. Bodies over 256 KB are refused.

Health check

Answers as long as the process serves requests. It does not touch the store.

This document

The OpenAPI 3.1 description of this server's API. Public and cacheable: send the
`ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get `304 Not Modified` while it is unchanged.
